title: ModuleNotFoundError in GCP after trying to sumbit a job
question:
new to GCP, I am trying to submit a job inside Dataproc with a .py file & attached also pythonproject.zip file (it is a project) but I am getting the below error ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pythonproject'

Below is the .py file that I upload:

from pythonproject.main import main
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

& below the main.py (inside the .zip file):

def main():
    print("Hello all!")

It is just a test case to understand in general if this is feasible in GCP & adjust our solution.

My archive structure is (after unzip it):

Python_Proj
    |--pythonproject
      |--main.py
      |--idea
         |--workspace
       
    |--idea
      |--gitignore
      |--workspace.xml

I am submitting this job inside a cluster that is already running & using the "Sumbit Job". I have already upload the .zip file & the .py file that I mentioned in the bucket ofc. The main file is upload it in Main py file with the gs://..../driver.py & the .zip in Archive files with the gs://...../Python_Proj.zip
answer:
In this situation, the ModuleNotFoundError occurred because the Python runtime couldn't locate the pythonproject module.

In Dataproc, you must explicitly include your zip of Python modules—via the --py-files flag (gcloud/CLI) or the "Archive files" field in the console so it’s added to the PYTHONPATH.

The archive’s structure must also match the expected module path (e.g., pythonproject/main.py under the root of the zip).

Confirm the module is referenced correctly (no extra folders inside the zip) and that the job submission flags include the zip. This approach aligns with Dataproc's official job submission instructions.

1. Restructure ZIP if needed:

Root of ZIP:
pythonproject/
    main.py

2. Submit job correctly, for example using CLI:

gcloud dataproc jobs submit pyspark \
  --cluster=CLUSTER_NAME \
  --region=REGION \
  --py-files=gs://BUCKET/Python_Proj.zip \
  gs://BUCKET/driver.py

3. Or via Console:

In "Submit Job" section:

  • Set driver.py as main.

  • Provide Python_Proj.zip as "Archive files".

4. Verify via logs if the path is in the runtime environment or explicitly print sys.path.
